subject.title: fix(qqbot): bind direct C2C fallback approvals to trusted actor identity

question: For direct QQBot C2C fallback callbacks, must privileged approval authority always come from a concrete `allowFrom` or `execApprovals.approvers` identity, or may the authenticated private-chat sender approve by default?
rationale: The patch’s tests establish a permanent privileged-action boundary, while the linked report expects a private-conversation Allow click to work without documenting whether a concrete trusted identity was configured.

options.title: Require Explicit Identity
options.body: Keep the fail-closed rule, reproduce explicit identity matching, and improve setup or diagnostics for users lacking a concrete approver.

options.title: Trust C2C Sender
options.body: Allow the authenticated direct-chat sender to approve implicitly, accepting the broader privilege boundary and adding targeted security proof.

options.title: Require Exec Approvers
options.body: Remove command-allowlist fallback for direct approvals and require `execApprovals.approvers` as the sole privileged identity source.

recommendation.title: Require Explicit Identity
recommendation.body: Keep the fail-closed rule, reproduce explicit identity matching, and improve setup or diagnostics for users lacking a concrete approver.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged and recently refined the existing QQBot approval-authorization contract and its documentation.
